title: Mandhana Takes Charge as BCCI Asks Harmanpreet to Mentor New Captain
excerpt: BCCI president Mithun Manhas wants Harmanpreet Kaur to guide new all-format captain Smriti Mandhana the way Dhoni guided Kohli — starting with the Zimbabwe series on October 16.
body:
• Smriti Mandhana, 30, has taken over as India's all-format women's captain after Harmanpreet Kaur, 37, stepped down — and the BCCI wants Kaur to stay on as a player and mentor her successor.
  • BCCI president Mithun Manhas cited India's men's tradition of senior-guided transitions, the model in which M.S. Dhoni guided new captain Virat Kohli, and said Harmanpreet will be an asset for Mandhana.
  • Mandhana's first full-time assignment starts October 16: a three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe in Raipur, followed by three ODIs in Vadodara.
  • Kaur leaves the captaincy with a maiden ODI World Cup title in 2025, Asian Games gold in 2026, and a record 155 T20Is as captain.

The newest development in India's women's captaincy transition is the mentoring plan around it. BCCI president Mithun Manhas has said Smriti Mandhana, newly appointed as India's all-format captain, will benefit from Harmanpreet Kaur's guidance as she settles into the role — explicitly invoking the men's precedent in which M.S. Dhoni guided Virat Kohli after handing over the captaincy, according to Cricket Addictor's report of Manhas's Sportstar interview and India Today.

Mandhana, 30, took over after Kaur, 37, stepped down earlier, the BCCI announced, in a decision first shared by Kaur in a social media post. Kaur made clear she will continue playing. Mandhana said in a BCCI statement that leading India was a special honour she would value deeply, according to SuperSport.

"I have always believed that the baton should be passed on when you have somebody senior around to guide them"

— Mithun Manhas, BCCI President

Why the board wants Kaur in the dressing room

Manhas told Sportstar that Indian cricket has benefited from keeping experienced players around new captains, because captaincy brings moments of confusion where a senior voice helps. He said this pattern of transformation has helped Indian cricket in a big way, and that Harmanpreet will be an asset for Smriti in exactly those decision moments. Reports of the interview note he pointed to the men's lineage — Sourav Ganguly, Dhoni and Kohli each benefited from experienced leaders around them — as the template the board wants repeated.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=3mBNBNv5V_0

The timing is deliberate. Kaur's leadership had been discussed at a BCCI review meeting after India's second successive group-stage exit from the T20 World Cup in June, SuperSport reported, even though she had led India to Asian Games gold in Japan and, last year, to the country's first women's global title at the ODI World Cup.

Two records, one handover

Kaur's tenure is the most decorated in Indian women's cricket. She captained India in 155 T20Is, 51 ODIs and five Tests, winning 126 of 211 matches across formats, and became the first captain in international cricket, male or female, to lead a team in more than 150 T20Is. She began as T20I captain in 2016 and took the Test and ODI teams in 2022 after Mithali Raj retired. Her sides reached the 2020 T20 World Cup final, won silver at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, won the 2025 ODI World Cup on home soil by beating South Africa in the final — making her only the third Indian captain after Kapil Dev and Dhoni to win a 50-over World Cup — and defended the Asian Games title in 2026.

Mandhana arrives with her own credentials. She has played nine Tests, 120 ODIs and 179 T20 Internationals since her 2013 debut, served as vice-captain for several years, captained India in 18 T20Is and four ODIs, and led Royal Challengers Bengaluru to two Women's Premier League titles in four years. At the Asian Games she made a 45-ball 79 in the final against Sri Lanka.

What happens next

Mandhana's first full-time assignment is immediate: a three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe in Raipur starting October 16, followed by three ODIs in Vadodara, with Kaur expected in the squad as a senior batter rather than in the stands. The open question the mentoring model has to answer is the one that ended Kaur's tenure — India's T20 World Cup record, with no title and two straight group-stage exits despite the WPL era. If Dhoni-for-Kohli is the template, success will be measured by whether Mandhana makes the hard calls herself while Kaur's experience is still on the field beside her.
